variants.headline: A new government takes shape
variants.sub: The colony has a newly formed government.
variants.body:
A new government has been formed in {colony}. Its formation establishes an administration; it does not establish the success of its future decisions. In considering {target}, the useful distinction is between assembling a government and meeting the obligations that come with governing.

An administration is necessary machinery, but its formation is not itself an economic programme. Business readers should assess specific decisions when they exist rather than price in a collection of assumptions. Confidence should attach to competent conduct, not simply to the completion of a political arrangement.

We welcome the contribution of {target}. Forming an administration is a legitimate achievement, and it deserves recognition without requiring us to pretend that every future difficulty has already been solved. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.

variants.sub: Government formation has produced a new administration in {colony}.

variants.sub: A new government has been formed in {colony}.
